chapter_title: Chương 38: 0038 [Huyền Thoại Vực Sâu, Sắp Ra Mắt]

segments.title: Chương 38: 0038 [Huyền Thoại Vực Sâu, Sắp Ra Mắt]
segments.content:
Other than Xie Yang and Tao Xue, no one at school knew about the private server.

For the past few days, Chen Guiliang had been going to the internet cafe every day at noon and in the evening to browse the forums for an hour.

He monitored public opinion constantly. As soon as he detected any potential problems, he immediately had Yang Yuhui lead the astroturfing team to guide the conversation. If a topic was difficult to guide, he would have Tao Chenggang update the "development log," releasing information about the private server's production progress to divert attention.

Every time he went to the internet cafe, Xie Yang would tag along eagerly, witnessing Chen Guiliang's operations firsthand.

Xie Yang was stunned by what he saw!

In the blink of an eye, it was November 28th, Friday.

Tonight at eight, the Abyss private server would go live on time.

At noon, in the internet cafe.

Xie Yang was browsing the forums and said to Chen Guiliang, "The netizens are so enthusiastic. They can't wait."

Chen Guiliang sent Tao Chenggang a QQ message: "What's the total number of game downloads across all the major forums?"

"I put it up at nine this morning, and so far only a little over two hundred people have downloaded it," Tao Chenggang said, worried. "Don't tell me the players are all talk, and they won't actually log into the game?"

"They will. The download peak hasn't arrived yet," Chen Guiliang said. "I'm more worried about the server capacity being insufficient. How many internet cafes are we cooperating with now?"

Tao Chenggang replied, "Including the local ones in Longdu City, there are 52 internet cafes in total. Inside a single cafe, a private server usually only has three to five people online at the same time, ten-plus at most. For 52 internet cafes, a good estimate for concurrent users would be three to four hundred people."

After repeated discussions between Chen Guiliang, Tao Chenggang, Yang Yuhui, and Feng Tao, they decided to open five servers directly this time, each capable of accommodating 1,000 players.

This approach didn't really fit the nature of a private server.

First, when a new version of a private server went live, it usually only opened one or two servers.

Second, each server had a maximum capacity of four to five hundred people; some private servers could only hold two to three hundred.

But the netizens on the major gaming forums were too enthusiastic, forcing Tao Chenggang to rent more servers, leaving enough space for 5,000 concurrent players.

This was a terrifying number.

One must remember that after a month of closed beta and extensive promotional campaigns, Fantasy Westward Journey's concurrent player count had only just broken 60,000 more than half a month after its official launch.

This was just a private server, yet they were reserving server capacity for 5,000 players. If word got out, people would laugh at them for being delusional.

At this moment, both Chen Guiliang and Tao Chenggang were worried.

Chen Guiliang was worried the servers wouldn't be enough, causing lag and preventing players from playing properly.

Tao Chenggang was worried the players would be no-shows, wasting the money spent on renting the servers.

"Let's go." Chen Guiliang went to the counter to log off.

Xie Yang quickly followed, saying, "I'm not going home this weekend. I'll stick with you and help run the private server!"

"Sure, I'll bring you along then," Chen Guiliang agreed.

It was the end of the month, so the third-year high school students got a two-day break, making it convenient for students from villages and towns to go home and get their living expenses.

In the second semester of the third year, time would become even tighter: a half-day off on normal weekends, and a one-day break on the weekend at the end of the month.

On the way back to school, Tao Xue called. "Big Nephew, let's take a taxi together after school this afternoon. My brother said he'll reimburse the fare."

"Let's wait at the school gate then. I'll call you," Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Xue chuckled, "I'll wait for you. Haha, our last class on Friday is PE."

After a few more words, Chen Guiliang hung up.

A bus drove by, and he saw Bian Guanyue sitting by the window, smiling and waving at him.

He walked back to school and entered the classroom.

Bian Guanyue was already studying, asking her deskmate Wu Meng for help with a math problem.

"Morning," Chen Guiliang said as he passed the first row.

Bian Guanyue looked up and asked Chen Guiliang, "Want some small potatoes?"

Wu Meng also looked up, a shy smile on her face, before continuing to explain the problem.

Chen Guiliang speared a piece of potato with a toothpick, popped it into his mouth without touching his teeth, and conveniently stuck the toothpick back in. "Tastes pretty good."

"Bought them at the school gate," Bian Guanyue said.

Xie Yang already saw Bian Guanyue as his future sister-in-law, so she wasn't an outsider. He helped himself to a piece of potato as well.

Returning to his seat, Chen Guiliang immediately started on his practice problems.

His academic progress was quite good.

Although he spent two to three hours every day discussing the private server's operations, Chen Guiliang paid close attention in class and did as many practice sheets as he could afterwards.

Every morning, he would memorize 10 English words, and then review them again in the evening.

He had the memory of a seventeen or eighteen-year-old and the comprehension of a forty-year-old. Moreover, he had learned this material before, so a quick review was enough to jog his memory.

He was mastering new knowledge points every day.

Making steady progress!

Chen Guiliang was soon immersed in the ocean of knowledge, but Xie Yang couldn't stop thinking about the private server going live tonight.

It was as if there were nails on his stool. The guy just couldn't sit still. He went over to Chen Guiliang and said, "You're still in the mood to do practice problems?"

Chen Guiliang was flipping through his history textbook, writing answers on a practice sheet while memorizing the key points for this long-answer question. "If you don't take your third year of high school seriously, are you planning on repeating it?"

"Shouldn't you be more focused on the private server? That's a man's career!" Xie Yang said anxiously.

Chen Guiliang retorted, "How can I focus on it now? By sitting in the classroom and worrying?"

Xie Yang suggested, "Why don't we skip class this afternoon and go to the internet cafe to keep an eye on those forums?"

"No need. We can just wait until after school," Chen Guiliang said, continuing with his problems.

Xie Yang sat next to Chen Guiliang for a few minutes, felt bored, and looked over at his other roommates. He discovered that, except for him, all the guys from 302 were actually studying!

Even Xu Haibo, who was addicted to novels, had started renting them much less frequently after the teachers began their review lessons.

A sense of guilt suddenly washed over Xie Yang.

Everyone was studying, and he was the only one still fooling around.

He hurried back to his seat, took out a few sets of practice sheets, and randomly picked one to work on slowly.

Xie Yang was actually very smart. He had ranked in the top 200 in the city for his high school entrance exam and was placed in the best experimental Class 1 in his first year. It was only because of his addiction to novels and games that he was forced to choose the liberal arts track in his second year.

At his craziest, Xie Yang had spent two consecutive weeks pulling all-nighters at the internet cafe, sleeping through all his classes during the day.

All-nighters were cheap, 5 yuan for a whole night, and sometimes he could even get an extra hour or two for free.

Even though he didn't listen in class at all and copied all his daily homework, Xie Yang could still comfortably get into a second-tier university.

Yet Yang Hao, the most hardworking one in Dorm 302, had an off day and ended up in a third-tier university…

After patiently finishing a set of practice sheets, Xie Yang went over to Chen Guiliang again. "Why don't you call Boss Tao again and ask him what the situation is?"

Chen Guiliang was exasperated. "You're more anxious than I am."

"I'm not anxious," Xie Yang said with an awkward smile.

The guy went back to his problems again, turning to look at Chen Guiliang from time to time. He felt a growing admiration in his heart: Big Bro Chen is the one who does great things, his expression unchanging even as Mount Tai crumbles before him. I must also cultivate this kind of calm demeanor. I am not anxious, I am not anxious. Do the problems!

Finally, the bell rang for the end of school.

Xie Yang stood up impatiently and yelled at Chen Guiliang, "Let's go, let's go!"

Chen Guiliang slowly tidied his desk, stuffed a few sets of practice sheets into his backpack, and was dragged out of the classroom by Xie Yang.

Zheng Feng, on the other hand, quickly ran over to Bian Guanyue.

Zheng Feng was the happiest about the seating change. He felt his chance had come again—Chen Guiliang couldn't be deskmates with Bian Guanyue anymore, but he could continue to walk her home after school.

Chen Guiliang actually admired this guy quite a bit.

Because when Zheng Feng waited for Bian Guanyue at the bus stop every day, he actually used the waiting time to squat by the roadside and do practice problems. He had somehow managed to both pursue a girl and study at the same time.

"Are you guys in a hurry?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Xie Yang continued to drag Chen Guiliang along. "We have important business to attend to!"

Zheng Feng seized the opportunity to say to Bian Guanyue, "They're definitely going to the internet cafe to play games."

Bian Guanyue didn't respond.

They quickly reached the school gate. Chen Guiliang called Tao Xue, "Where are you? It's full of people here, I can't see you."

On the last Friday of every month, at least four or five thousand students went home (the entire school had nearly 6,000 students).

"Here, here!"

Tao Xue was already submerged in the crowd. She stepped onto the green belt by the roadside, jumping up and down, waving and shouting.

Chen Guiliang and Xie Yang walked over to meet her.

Tao Xue said, "It's hard to get a taxi. Let's walk for a bit first."

There were simply too many students waiting for transportation. Buses arrived one after another, quickly filled up with students, and struggled to drive away.

Struggled, because of the traffic jam.

There were private cars picking up children, and illegally operating vans, all jammed together in a mess. Even making a U-turn was extremely difficult.

The three of them walked toward the street with all the internet cafes, and soon came across a taxi heading towards the school.

"Sir, to the city center!" Tao Xue said, getting into the front passenger seat.

The driver thought he had misheard and kindly reminded her, "It's at least 25 yuan on the meter from here to the city center. Also, I don't take the county road."

"Just drive, someone's paying for it," Tao Xue said, setting her brother up with righteous indignation.

"Hold on tight!"

The driver started the meter and stepped on the gas, simultaneously yanking the steering wheel to make a U-turn.

When Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue had taken the county road, the ride to the city center took three hours. This driver sped down the provincial highway, taking only half an hour. It felt like he was driving on an expressway.

"Bro, we're here."

"Go wait at Lin's Third Stir-Fry. I booked two tables."

A little over ten minutes later, Tao Chenggang arrived at the small restaurant in a whirlwind with eight or nine people.

Yang Yuhui was always a chatterbox. The moment he saw Chen Guiliang, he slapped his shoulder and exclaimed, "Damn, not bad! You turned into a handsome guy in just half a month!"

Tao Xue stood to the side and said, "When I saw him a few days ago, I thought I'd mistaken him for someone else."

As she spoke, she tilted her head and looked Chen Guiliang over again.

"In terms of handsomeness, I'm still a bit lacking compared to Brother Yang," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Yang Yuhui was extremely pleased to hear this and laughed heartily. "Not bad, you've got good taste. Your uncle, on the other hand, is no good. He always says I'm ugly."

Feng Tao said, "Handsome my ass."

Tao Chenggang smiled and shook Chen Guiliang's hand. "The various armies have finally joined forces. Let's make it a big night tonight!"

"Brother Gang, this is my good friend, Xie Yang. He's been helping post on the forums these past few days," Chen Guiliang introduced.

Xie Yang quickly greeted him, "Hello, President Tao."

Tao Chenggang shook his hand enthusiastically. "Guiliang's brother is my brother. Work hard, and I'll give you a red envelope later!"

Xie Yang was overwhelmed by the favor. He was just a poor student and didn't expect to be valued so highly by the boss.

Tao Chenggang then introduced the others.

Two of them were the network administrators from when he opened his first internet cafe; they had been with Tao Chenggang for two or three years.

Another three were the lead astroturfers selected by Yang Yuhui from his studio.

The remaining two were Tao Chenggang's former neighbors and childhood friends, who were currently idling away in a state-owned enterprise on the verge of bankruptcy.

Two dining tables were moved and pushed together. Just as a cold dish was served, Tao Chenggang raised his glass and said, "No alcohol today. Let's toast our brothers with tea instead. Here's to our private server being packed every day!"

"Cheers!"

Before Tao Chenggang could even drink his tea, the person left on duty called. "President Tao, the number of game downloads has exploded! It's already passed eight hundred!"

"Great! You keep watch. I'll have someone bring you back some good food," Tao Chenggang said, even more excited.

He hung up and said to Chen Guiliang, "The total downloads across the major private server forums have already passed eight hundred."

Chen Guiliang mused, "This is the time when office workers are heading home. In big cities, the commute time is even longer, so the peak download period hasn't actually arrived yet. I'm worried that a server capacity of 5,000 might not be enough."

"How is that possible?" Yang Yuhui said. "Some official games only have five or six thousand concurrent players. Anything that breaks ten thousand is already considered a popular game."

Tao Chenggang said, "It's too late to rent more servers now."

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's just hope it doesn't lag."

In this era, game queuing systems already existed, but they were considered "cutting-edge" technology and were very immature.

Chen Guiliang's private server, of course, couldn't have a queue.

If a huge crowd of players were to flood in at the same time, the scene would be too beautiful to imagine...

Three meals a day, yet you only update twice.
